## Chapter 1: General Provisions

### Section 1: Scope and Terminology

#### Art. 1. Purpose
The Penal Code shall define the punishments Administrators are required to punish members for violations of the Public Code.

#### Art. 2. Scope
The Penal Code shall apply to all members of the server.

#### Art. 3. Discord Terms of Service and Community Guidelines
Members of Administration may ensure contents and behaviours comply with Discord's ToS and Community Guidelines, but can only be punished as defined in this Penal Code. For any behaviours or contents that violates Discord ToS or Community Guidelines that are undefined and / or not criminalised in this Penal Code, consult to the Head Administrator or Director.

#### Art. 4. Definitions
<sup>1</sup> For the purposes of this Code, the following terms shall be defined as:\
a. *interactions* means any interaction between members that are:
  1. Text messages;
  2. Voice messages;
  3. Video call;
  4. Livestreams; and / or
  5. Voice call.

b. *media* means any content or visual/auditory that can be perceived, accessed, or viewed by another member.

c. *personal information* means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. This includes but not limited to someone's age, legal name, and home address.

## Chapter 2: Specific Provisions

### Section 1: Common Behaviours

#### Art. 5 Ping abuse
<sup>1</sup> Ping abuse shall be defined as pinging another member without their consent and that serves no purpose and is purely intended to annoy or harass.

<sup>2</sup> A member repeatedly pinging another member in large amounts shall receive:\
a. a five (5) minute timeout on the first offence;\
b. subsequent offences or more shall raise the duration in minutes by multiplying the last time out duration by 2;\
c. if they persist after their timeout with the duration of 1 week or more, they shall be kicked.

#### Art. 6. Spamming
<sup>1</sup> Spamming is prohibited if it:
a. disrupts anyone’s ongoing conversation of the channel(s) being spammed; and / or
b. clogs a channel with meaningless and / or repeated content

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall be punished by timeout, with the duration under an Administrator's discretion, maximum three (3) days.

<sup>3</sup> Above three (3) repeated offences shall be punishable by a kick.

<sup>4</sup> Administrators may delete spam contents if requested.

#### Art. 7. Advertising or self-promotion
<sup>1</sup> Any kinds of advertising or self-promotion shall only be punishable if:
a. the advertising is constant and/or disruptive to other members; and / or
b. the advertiser’s sole intention in the server is to advertise.

<sup>2</sup> Any member violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a two (2) hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a four (4) hour timeout on the third offence;
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

### Section 2: Accounts and Identity

#### Art. 8 Personal information
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not share any documents containing personal identifiable information.

<sup>2</sup> Such information defined in paragraph 1 shall be deleted immediately, including from any moderation logs.

<sup>3</sup> Any user who shares any personal information of another individual without their consent shall be banned immediately.

#### Art. 9 Impersonation
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not impersonate with the intent to:
a. deceive or mislead others into believing they are another natural individual; and / or:
b. making false claims of that individual.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:\
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a kick on the second offence.

#### Art. 10 Alternative accounts
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not use alternative accounts to:\
a. gain an extra vote on a poll; and / or\
b. bypass punishments.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall be permanently banned along with their alternative accounts.

<sup>1</sup> Administrators shall immediately delete any of the contents defined from Article 12 trough 16 that constitutes a violation.

a. disrupts anyone’s ongoing conversation of the channel(s) being spammed; and / or
b. clogs a channel with meaningless and / or repeated content

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall be punished by timeout, with the duration under an Administrator's discretion, maximum three (3) days.

<sup>3</sup> Above three (3) repeated offences shall be punishable by a kick.

<sup>4</sup> Administrators may delete spam contents if requested.

#### Art. 7. Advertising or self-promotion
<sup>1</sup> Any kinds of advertising or self-promotion shall only be punishable if:
a. the advertising is constant and/or disruptive to other members; and / or

<sup>2</sup> Any member violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a two (2) hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a four (4) hour timeout on the third offence;

e. a kick on the fifth offence.

The incitement, endorsement, or encouragement to commit a violation of law, disrupt or threaten the order, peace, and unity of the server shall be punishable by no less than 1-week timeout and a 6000₣ fine.

b. *media* means any content or visual/auditory that can be perceived, accessed, or viewed by another member.

c. *personal information* means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person. This includes but not limited to someone's age, legal name, and home address.

## Title 2: Specific Provisions

### Section 1: Common Behaviours

#### Art. 5 Ping Abuse
<sup>1</sup> Ping abuse shall be defined as pinging another member without their consent and that serves no purpose and is purely intended to annoy or harass.

<sup>2</sup> A member repeatedly pinging another member in large amounts shall receive:\
a. a five (5) minute timeout on the first offence;\
b. subsequent offences or more shall raise the duration in minutes by multiplying the last time out duration by 2;\
c. if they persist after their timeout with the duration of 1 week or more, they shall be kicked.

#### Art. 6. Spamming
<sup>1</sup> Spamming is prohibited if it:
a. disrupts anyone’s ongoing conversation of the channel(s) being spammed; and / or
b. clogs a channel with meaningless and / or repeated content

<sup>2</sup> Violation of paragraph 1 shall be punished by timeout, with the duration under an Administrator's discretion, maximum three (3) days.

<sup>3</sup> Above three (3) repeated offences shall be punishable by a kick.

<sup>4</sup> Administrators may delete spam contents if requested.

#### Art. 7. Advertising or Self-promotion
<sup>1</sup> Any kinds of advertising or self-promotion shall only be punishable if:
a. the advertising is constant and/or disruptive to other members; and / or
b. the advertiser’s sole intention in the server is to advertise.

<sup>2</sup> Any member violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a two (2) hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a four (4) hour timeout on the third offence;
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

### Section 2: Accounts and Identity

#### Art. 8 Personal Information
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not share any documents containing personal identifiable information.

<sup>2</sup> Such information defined in paragraph 1 shall be deleted immediately, including from any moderation logs.

<sup>3</sup> Any user who shares personal information of other individuals without their consent shall be banned immediately.

#### Art. 9 Impersonation
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not impersonate with the intent to:
a. deceive or mislead others into believing they are another natural individual; and / or:
b. making false claims of that individual.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:\
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a kick on the second offence.

#### Art. 10 Alternative Accounts
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not use alternative accounts to:\
a. gain an extra vote on a poll; and / or\
b. bypass punishments.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall be permanently banned along with their alternative accounts.

#### Art. 11. Deletion of Contents
<sup>1</sup> Administrators shall immediately delete any of the contents defined from Article 12 trough 16 that constitutes a violation.

#### Art. 12 Files and Links
The sharing of files or other downloadable attachments containing malicious code, malware, viruses, trojans, ransomware, spyware, or keyloggers shall be punishable by an instant ban.

<sup>2</sup> Sharing links, drive folders, or external repositories that directly host or lead to malicious files or phishing pages is treated identically to direct file uploads and has the same punishment defined in paragraph 1.

<sup>3</sup> Files or attachments that are not necessarily harmful but cause temporary disruptions such as temporarily corrupting the rendering of the Discord application, the sender shall be warned. Repeated behaviours shall lead to a timeout. After four counts, the sender shall be kicked.

#### Art. 13 Non-consensual Romantic Pairings
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not pair, “ship”, or depict real individuals of the server in romantic and / or sexual contexts in any media or interaction, without prior explicit consent from any of the parties involved in the depiction.

<sup>2</sup> Members violating paragraph 1 shall receive:
a. a 24-hour timeout on the first offence; and:
b. a kick on the second offence.

<sup>3</sup> Such contents shall be removed upon request by any individuals depicted.

<sup>2</sup> The non-consensual application of behaviours defined in paragraph 1 onto other members shall constitute:
a. a 12-hour timeout on the first offence;
b. a kick on the second offence; and
c. a ban on the third offence.

<sup>3</sup> The presentation of media as a humorous image, macro, trend, or ‘meme’ does not grant exemption from the provisions of this Article.

#### Art. 15 Violence and Gore
<sup>1</sup> Members shall not post or have media that depicts:
a. extreme physical violence;
b. real footage of psychological harm;
c. sexual violence;
d. serious bodily injury; and
e. content fetishising these imagery.

<sup>2</sup> Violations of paragraph 1 are punishable by a permanent ban.

<sup>3</sup> The following does not constitute a violation if the sender is using a spoiler tag or in a dedicated NSFW channel:\
a. medias that depict surgical operations in a clinical context;\
b. medias depicting real war footages; and\
c. arts depicting violence and blood.

<sup>1</sup> Not Safe for Work, abbreviated as NSFW, shall be defined as anything which includes media or interactions; that is reasonably considered inappropriate, explicit, or intrusive to be viewed, heard, or engaged with in public spaces, workplaces, or shared social and domestic environments without the explicit consent or prior warning of those present.

<sup>2</sup> Members interacting in a way that depicts or implies an explicit sexual act shall receive:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 2-hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a 4-hour timeout on the third offence; and
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

a. a warning on the first offence to move their discussion to a designated channel for NSFW contents;
b. a 2-hour timeout on their second offence for failure to move their discussion;
c. a 12-hour timeout on their third offence; and
d. a kick on the fourth offence.

a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 4-hour timeout on the second through fourth offences; and
c. a kick on the fifth offence.

<sup>5</sup> Any depiction of explicit sexual acts, nudity, and adult novelties is punishable by:
a. a 24-hour timeout on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence;
c. a 1-week timeout on the fourth offence; and
d. a kick on the fifth offence.

<sup>6</sup> For the purposes of paragraph 4, prohibited depictions include, but are not limited to:

c. presence of fluids that is made for, during and / or as a result of sexual acts;
d. intentional physical contact of sex organs and other organs for sexual pleasure;
e. clothing specifically designed for sexual pleasure;
f. sexual acts done by other species besides humans; and
g. sexual organs clearly visible through clothing.

a. adult novelties that do not necessarily have the form of a sex organ; and
b. fine arts depicting nudity.

a. a warning on the first offence;

c. 1-day timeout on the third offence; and
d. a kick on the fourth violation.

a. buttocks;

laws.title: Penal Procedure Code
laws.content:
*(ProNaCo, PPC)*

The Director of Nirleka Studios,

based on Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 101),

decrees:

## Chapter 1: Scope of Application and Principles

### Art. 1 Scope of Application
<sup>1</sup> This Code regulates the prosecution and adjudication by members of Administration for offences under Server laws.

<sup>2</sup> The procedural regulations contained in other Server laws are reserved.

### Art. 2 Administration of penalties and measures
<sup>1</sup> The administration of penalties and measures is the responsibility solely of the authorities specified by law.

<sup>2</sup> Penal proceedings may be conducted and concluded only in the forms provided for by law.

## Chapter 2: Principles of Penal Procedure Laws

### Art. 3 Independence
Enforcing and judicial authorities are independent in applying the law and bound solely by the law.

### Art. 4 Principle of expeditiousness
<sup>1</sup> The Administration must start penal proceedings immediately and conclude them without unjustified delay.

<sup>2</sup> Where an accused is unavailable, penal proceedings must still continue, including:
a. the logging of the violation; and
b. any relevant procedures outlined by law.

### Art. 5 Obligation to act
Enforcing authorities are under the obligation to act according to law upon a violation of law.

### Art. 6 Principle of no judgment without a charge
An offence may only be judicially assessed if an enforcing authority has brought a related charge against a specific person in the competent judicial authority based on precisely described circumstances.

### Art. 7 Prohibition of double jeopardy
No person who has been convicted or acquitted in the Server by a final legally binding judgment may be prosecuted again for the same offence.

### Art. 8 Presumption of innocence and assessment of evidence
<sup>1</sup> Every person is presumed to be innocent until they have been convicted in a judgment that is final and legally binding.

<sup>2</sup> The judicial authority must be free to interpret the evidence in accordance with the views that it forms over the entire proceedings.

<sup>3</sup> Where there is insurmountable doubt whether the factual requirements of alleged offence have been fulfilled, the judicial authority shall proceed on the assumption that the circumstances more favourable to the accused occurred.

### Art. 9 Evidence
The enforcing authority bears the burden of establishing that a violation occurred.

### Art. 10 Case records
<sup>1</sup> Every judicial proceeding must receive a unique case identifier.

<sup>2</sup> The case record must contain, at minimum:
a. the case identifier;
b. the parties involved;
c. the challenged action or legal question;
d. the applicable law;
e. the material evidence;
f. the final decision; and
g. the reasoning supporting the decision.

<sup>3</sup> Judicial records must be maintained in an auditable format.

### Art. 11 Right to notice
A person must be informed what law and specific, relevant provisions they have been charged, acquitted, and punished for.

### Art. 12 Conflict of interest
Judicial authorities must not decide on a case in which they are personally involved.

## Chapter 3: The Authorities

#### Art. 13 Knowledge of the law
Administrators, including judicial and enforcing authorities, must be knowledgeable about the law

### Section 1: The Enforcing Authorities

#### Art. 14 The enforcing authorities
The enforcing authorities are:
a. members of the Administration's Executive Branch as defined in Section 2 of the Server Charter; and
b. their appointed staff.

### Section 2: The Judicial Authorities

#### Art. 15 The judicial authorities
<sup>1</sup> Judicial authority rests with the Secretary.

<sup>2</sup> Where the Secretary is not available or is a named party in a dispute, the Director may hold judicial authority.

#### Art. 16 Rule of necessity
Where both the Secretary and the Director are conflicted in a single matter, and no impartial authority is lawfully able to be assigned, the Director must issue a binding administrative decision to prevent a deadlock.

## Chapter 4: Penal Procedures

### Section 1: Procedures for Member Violations

#### Art. 17 Regular member
A regular member is a Server member holding no position in the Administration.

#### Art. 18 No judicial procedures
If a regular member violates a law, unless a law says otherwise, judicial procedures are not required.

#### Art. 19 Right of appeal
<sup>1</sup> Judicial proceedings are required if the affected member requests an appeal.

<sup>2</sup> Where a member is still serving their duration of punishment, proceedings must be conducted off-Server.

#### Art. 20 Enforcement
<sup>1</sup> Upon a regular member violating a law, enforcing authorities must immediately:
a. impose a measure outlined by law; and
b. document relevant administrative and moderation actions.

### Section 2: Procedures for Violations by the Administration

#### Art. 21 Suspension
<sup>1</sup> A suspension removes administrative permissions normally granted to an Administrator for their position, and they may not exercise any administrative powers during the suspension period.

<sup>2</sup> If substantial evidence of a grave violation of law is reported to a Secretary, or other superior Administrators, the accused Administrator must be suspended.

<sup>3</sup> Judicial authorities must not impose a ban as a measure against an Administrator if the applicable law does not explicitly state such measure.

#### Art. 22 Violations from administrators
<sup>1</sup> Judicial proceedings are required for Administrators who committed violations of law.

<sup>2</sup> Judicial authorities have broad discretion to raise the measure for violations committed by Administrators based on their seniority.

## Chapter 5: Appeals

### Art. 23 Appeals
<sup>1</sup> A member affected by a moderation or administrative action may appeal that action to judicial authorities.

<sup>2</sup> An appeal may challenge:
a. whether the alleged conduct occurred;
b. whether the conduct constituted a violation of law;
c. whether the cited law was correctly interpreted or applied;
d. whether the penalty was lawful or proportionate; or
e. whether the procedure followed by Administration was lawful.

### Art. 24 Filing an appeal
<sup>1</sup> An appeal must identify:
a. the appellant;
b. the administrative action being challenged;
c. the law or decision concerned, where known;
d. the grounds of appeal; and
e. any evidence or information relied upon.

<sup>2</sup> An appeal must be concise and may be submitted in any reasonable format determined by the Secretary.

<sup>3</sup> Minor defects in an appeal must not result in its dismissal where the substance of the complaint can reasonably be understood.

## Chapter 6: Triage and Informal Resolution

### Art. 25 Screening and classification
<sup>1</sup> Upon receiving an appeal, the judicial authority must classify the matter as either:
a. a Summary Review, for minor infractions, clear errors, or routine moderation; or
b. a Formal Proceeding, for severe penalties, staff violations, or complex factual disputes.

<sup>2</sup> An appeal must be filed within 14 days of the penal measure being imposed. Late filings are dismissed as inadmissible unless extraordinary circumstances exist.

### Art. 26 Summary review procedure
<sup>1</sup> In a Summary Review, the judicial authority must examine the record provided by the appellant and the enforcing authority without opening formal hearings.

<sup>2</sup> If the judicial authority finds that a measure was unlawful, unsupported by evidence, or disproportionate, they must issue a summary order directing the enforcing authority to modify, commute, or immediately lift the measure.

<sup>3</sup> Enforcing authorities are bound to execute summary orders without delay.

## Chapter 7: Formal judicial proceedings

### Art. 27 Opening of proceedings
<sup>1</sup> Where a matter is designated for Formal Proceeding, the judicial authority must establish a secure, dedicated channel or ticket off-Server for the exchange of arguments and evidence.

<sup>2</sup> The filing of an appeal does not suspend the execution of the penalty unless the judicial authority grants a temporary stay.

### Art. 28 Evidence and submissions
<sup>1</sup> The enforcing authority has 48 hours to submit all logs, screenshots, and statement of facts establishing the violation.

<sup>2</sup> If the enforcing authority fails to submit sufficient evidence within the prescribed timeframe, the judicial authority must rule in favour of the appellant and dismiss the charges.

<sup>3</sup> The appellant must be given a single, structured opportunity to review the enforcing authority's evidence and submit a final rebuttal.

### Art. 29 Adjudication and ruling
<sup>1</sup> The judicial authority must issue a written judgment within 7 days of opening the proceeding.

<sup>2</sup> The judgment must contain:
a. a summary of the facts;
b. the relevant legal provisions applied;
c. the verdict (Upheld, Modified, or Overturned); and
d. the remedy or order, if applicable.

<sup>3</sup> Rulings issued by the competent judicial authority are final and binding on all members and Administration.


## Annex 1
The following acts are repealed:
a. SR 415 on Courts and Appeals Proceedings

Where both the Secretary and the Director are conflicted in a single matter, and no impartial authority is lawfully able to be assigned, the Director must issue a binding administrative decision to prevent a deadlock.

## Chapter 4: Penal Procedures

### Section 1: Procedures for Member Violations

#### Art. 17 Regular member
A regular member is a Server member holding no position in the Administration.

#### Art. 18 No judicial procedures
If a regular member violates a law, unless a law says otherwise, judicial procedures are not required.

#### Art. 19 Right of appeal
<sup>1</sup> Judicial proceedings are required if the affected member requests an appeal.

<sup>2</sup> Where a member is still serving their duration of punishment, proceedings must be conducted off-Server.

#### Art. 20 Enforcement
<sup>1</sup> Upon a regular member violating a law, enforcing authorities must immediately:
a. impose a measure outlined by law; and
b. document relevant administrative and moderation actions.

### Section 2: Procedures for Violations by the Administration

#### Art. 21 Suspension
<sup>1</sup> A suspension removes administrative permissions normally granted to an Administrator for their position, and they may not exercise any administrative powers during the suspension period.

<sup>2</sup> If substantial evidence of a grave violation of law is reported to a Secretary, or other superior Administrators, the accused Administrator must be suspended.

<sup>3</sup> Judicial authorities must not impose a ban as a measure against an Administrator if the applicable law does not explicitly state such measure.

#### Art. 22 Violations from administrators
<sup>1</sup> Judicial proceedings are required for Administrators who committed violations of law.

<sup>2</sup> Judicial authorities have broad discretion to raise the measure for violations committed by Administrators based on their seniority.

## Chapter 5: Appeals

### Art. 23 Appeals
<sup>1</sup> A member affected by a moderation or administrative action may appeal that action to judicial authorities.

<sup>2</sup> An appeal may challenge:
a. whether the alleged conduct occurred;
b. whether the conduct constituted a violation of law;
c. whether the cited law was correctly interpreted or applied;
d. whether the penalty was lawful or proportionate; or
e. whether the procedure followed by Administration was lawful.

### Art. 24 Filing an appeal
<sup>1</sup> An appeal must identify:
a. the appellant;
b. the administrative action being challenged;
c. the law or decision concerned, where known;
d. the grounds of appeal; and
e. any evidence or information relied upon.

<sup>2</sup> An appeal must be concise and may be submitted in any reasonable format determined by the Secretary.

<sup>3</sup> Minor defects in an appeal must not result in its dismissal where the substance of the complaint can reasonably be understood.

## Chapter 6: Triage and Informal Resolution

### Art. 25 Screening and classification
<sup>1</sup> Upon receiving an appeal, the judicial authority must classify the matter as either:
a. a Summary Review, for minor infractions, clear errors, or routine moderation; or
b. a Formal Proceeding, for severe penalties, staff violations, or complex factual disputes.

<sup>2</sup> An appeal must be filed within 14 days of the penal measure being imposed. Late filings are dismissed as inadmissible unless extraordinary circumstances exist.

### Art. 26 Summary review procedure
<sup>1</sup> In a Summary Review, the judicial authority must examine the record provided by the appellant and the enforcing authority without opening formal hearings.

<sup>2</sup> If the judicial authority finds that a measure was unlawful, unsupported by evidence, or disproportionate, they must issue a summary order directing the enforcing authority to modify, commute, or immediately lift the measure.

<sup>3</sup> Enforcing authorities are bound to execute summary orders without delay.

## Chapter 7: Formal judicial proceedings

### Art. 27 Opening of proceedings
<sup>1</sup> Where a matter is designated for Formal Proceeding, the judicial authority must establish a secure, dedicated channel or ticket off-Server for the exchange of arguments and evidence.

<sup>2</sup> The filing of an appeal does not suspend the execution of the penalty unless the judicial authority grants a temporary stay.

### Art. 28 Evidence and submissions
<sup>1</sup> The enforcing authority has 48 hours to submit all logs, screenshots, and statement of facts establishing the violation.

<sup>2</sup> If the enforcing authority fails to submit sufficient evidence within the prescribed timeframe, the judicial authority must rule in favour of the appellant and dismiss the charges.

<sup>3</sup> The appellant must be given a single, structured opportunity to review the enforcing authority's evidence and submit a final rebuttal.

### Art. 29 Adjudication and ruling
<sup>1</sup> The judicial authority must issue a written judgment within 7 days of opening the proceeding.

<sup>2</sup> The judgment must contain:
a. a summary of the facts;
b. the relevant legal provisions applied;
c. the verdict (Upheld, Modified, or Overturned); and
d. the remedy or order, if applicable.

<sup>3</sup> Rulings issued by the competent judicial authority are final and binding on all members and Administration.

*(ADC, AdminDisCo)*

*The Director of Nirleka Studios,*

based on Article 2 and 24 of the Server Charter (SR 101),

decrees:

## Chapter 1: General Provisions

### Section 1: Fundamentals

#### Art. 1 No penalty without a law
A penalty or measure may only be imposed for an act that has been expressly declared to be an offence by law.

#### Art. 2 Scope
<sup>1</sup> This Code applies to any offence committed by any Administrator on or after the date it comes into force.

<sup>2</sup> For offences committed before the date this Code comes into force, the regulations and penalties in effect at the time of the offence apply.

#### Art. 3 Prohibition of double jeopardy
No person who has been convicted or acquitted in the Server by a final legally binding judgment may be prosecuted again for the same offence.

#### Art. 4 An Administrator
An Administrator is a member of Administration, including the positions defined in Chapter 2 of the Server Charter (SR 101), and their appointed staff.

#### Art. 5 Equality
The persons subject to penal laws for the Administration remains subject to ordinary penal laws and other Server laws.

### Section 2: Intent and Negligence

#### Art. 6 Terms
<sup>1</sup> Unless the law expressly provides otherwise, an offence is punishable only if it is committed intentionally.

<sup>2</sup> A person commits an offence intentionally if they carry out the act with knowledge and intent. It is also intentional if the perpetrator considers the commission of the offence to be possible and accepts its occurrence.

<sup>3</sup> A person commits an offence negligently if they fail to consider or take into account the consequences of their conduct due to a breach of their duty of care. Negligence is inadvertent if the offender fails to exercise the caution to which they are obliged under the circumstances and according to their personal situation.

#### Art. 7 Mistake of fact
<sup>1</sup> If the offender acts under a mistaken appreciation of the facts, judicial authority must judge the act according to the facts as the offender believed them to be.

<sup>2</sup> If the offender could have avoided the mistake had they exercised due care, they are punishable for negligence if the negligent commission of the act is an offence.

#### Art. 8 Acts authorised by law
A person acts lawfully if their conduct is required or authorised by law, even if that conduct would otherwise constitute an offence under this Code or any other law.

### Section 3: Participation

#### Art. 9 Incitement and complicity
<sup>1</sup> A person who intentionally induces another person to commit an offence (inciter) is liable to the same penalty as the principal perpetrator.

<sup>2</sup> A person who intentionally assists another person in committing an offence (accomplice) is subject to a mitigated penalty.

#### Art. 10 Attempt
<sup>1</sup> An attempt occurs when a person initiates the execution of an offence but fails to complete it.

<sup>2</sup> An attempt is punishable only if the offence itself is punishable when committed intentionally. Judicial authority may mitigate the penalty for an attempted offence.

<sup>3</sup> A person who voluntarily abandons the execution of an offence or prevents its completion is punished for the attempt.

### Section 4: Terminology

#### Art. 11 Moderation action
<sup>1</sup> A moderation action is any exercise of administrative or technical power that restricts, alters, removes, or penalizes a member’s ability to participate, communicate, or access features within the Server.

<sup>2</sup> Moderation actions include, in particular:
a. timeouts, mutes, and suspensions;
b. the deletion, modification, or hiding of messages or content;
c. the revocation of permissions or roles; and
d. the imposition of fines, kicks, or bans.

## Chapter 2: Penalties and Measures

### Art. 12 Timeout
<sup>1</sup> A timeout deprives an Administrator of the ability to:
a. interact with other members on the Server;
b. alter any Server features or configurations; and
c. exercise any power or technical privilege attached to their position.

<sup>2</sup> A timeout must be imposed for a minimum duration of 1 hour and a maximum duration of 28 days.

<sup>3</sup> The native Discord timeout feature may be used to execute this measure.

### Art. 13 Suspension
<sup>1</sup> A suspension deprives an Administrator of the right to exercise any administrative, technical, or judicial power derived from their position for a specified period not exceeding 90 days.

<sup>2</sup> During a suspension, the Administrator retains their position but loses access to administrative channels, logs, and permission sets.

### Art. 14 Removal from position
<sup>1</sup> Removal from position consists of the permanent revocation of the Administrator’s specific role, title, and assigned duties within the Administration.

<sup>2</sup> A person removed from position under this Article may not be reappointed to an administrative role for a period of at least 4 months.

### Art. 15 Demotion
A demotion consists of stripping the Administrator of their current tier or rank and assigning them to a lower subordinate role within the Administration hierarchy.

### Art. 16 Fine
<sup>1</sup> A fine is a financial penalty imposing a fixed liability in Nirleka francs (₣) on the convicted Administrator, in accordance with Article 2, Paragraph 2 and Article 6 of the Economy Act (SR 610).

<sup>2</sup> The execution of a fine takes place through the immediate and automatic deduction of the specified amount from the Administrator’s account balance by the competent authority. If the account balance is insufficient to satisfy the full amount, the remaining sum constitutes a binding debt against the member, resulting in a negative balance.

<sup>3</sup> Unless an article in Chapter 3 explicitly provides for a fixed fine, a fine is imposed:
a. as a standalone penalty of not less than 100₣ and not more than 5,000₣; or
b. as a supplementary penalty alongside a timeout, suspension, or demotion.

<sup>4</sup> The authority determining the sentence assesses the amount of the fine taking into account:
a. the severity of the offence; and
b. the financial situation of the offender at the time of judgment.

<sup>5</sup> If the debt remains outstanding for more than 14 days following a final judgment, the authority may convert the unpaid balance into a suspension at a rate of 1 day of suspension for every 100₣ outstanding, up to a maximum of 30 days.

## Chapter 3: Offences

### Section 1: Offences Against Administrative Authority and Duties

#### Art. 17 Neglect of duty
An Administrator who, through gross negligence, fails to perform an administrative duty assigned to them by law or order, causing disruption to Server operations or administration, is punished with a timeout not exceeding 7 days, a fine not exceeding 1,000₣, or both.

#### Art. 18 Disobeying a lawful order
An Administrator who intentionally refuses or fails to execute a lawful directive or order issued by a superior administrative authority is punished with a timeout not exceeding 14 days, a fine not exceeding 2,500₣, or suspension.

#### Art. 19 Execution of an unlawful order
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator who executes an order knowing, or under circumstances where they ought to have known, that the order violates Server law is punished with a timeout not exceeding 7 days or a fine not exceeding 1,000₣.

<sup>2</sup> If the Administrator acted under direct threat of retaliatory administrative action by a superior, the penalty may be mitigated or waived.

#### Art. 20 Excess of official authority
An Administrator who exercises an administrative, technical, or judicial power not granted to them by law, or who exercises a power in direct violation of express statutory restrictions, is punished with a suspension, a fine not exceeding 5,000₣, or removal from position.

### Section 2: Offences Against Administrative Records and Integrity

#### Art. 21 Failure to log moderation actions
An Administrator who carries out a moderation action without recording the required entry in the official audit log or designated record within the prescribed timeframe is punished with a fine not exceeding 500₣.

#### Art. 22 Tampering with moderation logs
An Administrator who intentionally alters, falsifies, deletes, or conceals an official audit log, moderation record, or administrative entry is punished with a suspension, a fine not exceeding 5,000₣, or removal from position.

#### Art. 23 Bribery
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator who solicits, accepts, or promises to accept Nirleka francs, real-world currency, or any other personal advantage in exchange for performing or omitting an official administrative act is punished with removal from position and a fine of not less than 2,000₣.

<sup>2</sup> Whoever offers, promises, or grants an advantage to an Administrator to influence their official conduct is subject to penalties under ordinary Server law.

#### Art. 24 Abuse of power
An Administrator who intentionally uses their administrative position, access privileges, or technical powers to secure an unlawful advantage for themselves or a third party, or to intentionally cause harm to a member, is punished with a suspension, a fine not exceeding 5,000₣, or removal from position.

### Section 3: Offences Against Member Rights and Public Order

#### Art. 25 Unlawful moderation
An Administrator who intentionally imposes a ban, kick, timeout, or other restriction on a member without a factual basis or legal ground provided by Server law is punished with a timeout not exceeding 14 days, a fine not exceeding 2,500₣, or suspension.

#### Art. 26 Targeted harassment and personal hostility
An Administrator who uses their official position or public communication channels to repeatedly insult, intimidate, dox, or publish private personal details of a member or another Administrator without consent is punished with a suspension, a fine not exceeding 5,000₣, or removal from position.

#### Art. 27 Instigation of public disorder
An Administrator who publicly incites members to violate Server law, disobey administrative orders, or disrupt official Server functions is punished with a suspension or removal from position.

An Administrator who publicly incites members to violate Server law, disobey administrative orders, or disrupt official Server functions is punished with a suspension or removal from position.

*(ADC, AdminDisCo)

*The Director of Nirleka Studios,*

based on Article 2 and 24 of the Server Charter (SR 101),

decrees:

## Chapter 1: General Provisions

### Section 1: Fundamentals

#### Art. 1 No penalty without a law
A penalty or measure may only be imposed for an act that has been expressly declared to be an offence by law.

#### Art. 2 Scope
<sup>1</sup> This Code applies to any offence committed by any Administrator on or after the date it comes into force.

<sup>2</sup> For offences committed before the date this Code comes into force, the regulations and penalties in effect at the time of the offence apply.

#### Art. 3 Prohibition of double jeopardy
No person who has been convicted or acquitted in the Server by a final legally binding judgment may be prosecuted again for the same offence.

#### Art. 4 An Administrator
An Administrator is a member of Administration, including the positions defined in Chapter 2 of the Server Charter (SR 101), and their appointed staff.

#### Art. 5 Equality
The persons subject to penal laws for the Administration remains subject to ordinary penal laws and other Server laws.

### Section 2: Intent and Negligence

#### Art. 6 Terms
<sup>1</sup> Unless the law expressly provides otherwise, an offence is punishable only if it is committed intentionally.

<sup>2</sup> A person commits an offence intentionally if they carry out the act with knowledge and intent. It is also intentional if the perpetrator considers the commission of the offence to be possible and accepts its occurrence.

<sup>3</sup> A person commits an offence negligently if they fail to consider or take into account the consequences of their conduct due to a breach of their duty of care. Negligence is inadvertent if the offender fails to exercise the caution to which they are obliged under the circumstances and according to their personal situation.

#### Art. 7 Mistake of fact
<sup>1</sup> If the offender acts under a mistaken appreciation of the facts, judicial authority must judge the act according to the facts as the offender believed them to be.

<sup>2</sup> If the offender could have avoided the mistake had they exercised due care, they are punishable for negligence if the negligent commission of the act is an offence.

#### Art. 8 Acts authorised by law
A person acts lawfully if their conduct is required or authorised by law, even if that conduct would otherwise constitute an offence under this Code or any other law.

### Section 3: Participation

#### Art. 9 Incitement and complicity
<sup>1</sup> A person who intentionally induces another person to commit an offence (inciter) is liable to the same penalty as the principal perpetrator.

<sup>2</sup> A person who intentionally assists another person in committing an offence (accomplice) is subject to a mitigated penalty.

#### Art. 10 Attempt
<sup>1</sup> An attempt occurs when a person initiates the execution of an offence but fails to complete it.

<sup>2</sup> An attempt is punishable only if the offence itself is punishable when committed intentionally. Judicial authority may mitigate the penalty for an attempted offence.

<sup>3</sup> A person who voluntarily abandons the execution of an offence or prevents its completion is punished for the attempt.

### Section 4: Terminology

#### Art. 11 Moderation action
<sup>1</sup> A moderation action is any exercise of administrative or technical power that restricts, alters, removes, or penalizes a member’s ability to participate, communicate, or access features within the Server.

<sup>2</sup> Moderation actions include, in particular:
a. timeouts, mutes, and suspensions;
b. the deletion, modification, or hiding of messages or content;
c. the revocation of permissions or roles; and
d. the imposition of fines, kicks, or bans.

## Chapter 2: Penalties and Measures

### Art. 12 Timeout
<sup>1</sup> A timeout deprives an Administrator of the ability to:
a. interact with other members on the Server;
b. alter any Server features or configurations; and
c. exercise any power or technical privilege attached to their position.

<sup>2</sup> A timeout must be imposed for a minimum duration of 1 hour and a maximum duration of 28 days.

<sup>3</sup> The native Discord timeout feature may be used to execute this measure.

### Art. 13 Suspension
<sup>1</sup> A suspension deprives an Administrator of the right to exercise any administrative, technical, or judicial power derived from their position for a specified period not exceeding 90 days.

<sup>2</sup> During a suspension, the Administrator retains their position but loses access to administrative channels, logs, and permission sets.

### Art. 14 Removal from position
<sup>1</sup> Removal from position consists of the permanent revocation of the Administrator’s specific role, title, and assigned duties within the Administration.

<sup>2</sup> A person removed from position under this Article may not be reappointed to an administrative role for a period of at least 4 months.

### Art. 15 Demotion
A demotion consists of stripping the Administrator of their current tier or rank and assigning them to a lower subordinate role within the Administration hierarchy.

### Art. 16 Fine
<sup>1</sup> A fine is a financial penalty imposing a fixed liability in Nirleka francs (₣) on the convicted Administrator, in accordance with Article 2, Paragraph 2 and Article 6 of the Economy Act (SR 610).

<sup>2</sup> The execution of a fine takes place through the immediate and automatic deduction of the specified amount from the Administrator’s account balance by the competent authority. If the account balance is insufficient to satisfy the full amount, the remaining sum constitutes a binding debt against the member, resulting in a negative balance.

<sup>3</sup> Unless an article in Chapter 3 explicitly provides for a fixed fine, a fine is imposed:
a. as a standalone penalty of not less than 100₣ and not more than 5,000₣; or
b. as a supplementary penalty alongside a timeout, suspension, or demotion.

<sup>4</sup> The authority determining the sentence assesses the amount of the fine taking into account:
a. the severity of the offence; and
b. the financial situation of the offender at the time of judgment.

<sup>5</sup> If the debt remains outstanding for more than 14 days following a final judgment, the authority may convert the unpaid balance into a suspension at a rate of 1 day of suspension for every 100₣ outstanding, up to a maximum of 30 days.

## Chapter 3: Offences

### Section 1: Offences Against Administrative Authority and Duties

#### Art. 17 Neglect of duty
An Administrator who, through gross negligence, fails to perform an administrative duty assigned to them by law or order, causing disruption to Server operations or administration, is punished with a timeout not exceeding 7 days, a fine not exceeding 1,000₣, or both.

#### Art. 18 Disobeying a lawful order
An Administrator who intentionally refuses or fails to execute a lawful directive or order issued by a superior administrative authority is punished with a timeout not exceeding 14 days, a fine not exceeding 2,500₣, or suspension.

#### Art. 19 Execution of an unlawful order
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator who executes an order knowing, or under circumstances where they ought to have known, that the order violates Server law is punished with a timeout not exceeding 7 days or a fine not exceeding 1,000₣.

<sup>2</sup> If the Administrator acted under direct threat of retaliatory administrative action by a superior, the penalty may be mitigated or waived.

#### Art. 20 Excess of official authority
An Administrator who exercises an administrative, technical, or judicial power not granted to them by law, or who exercises a power in direct violation of express statutory restrictions, is punished with a suspension, a fine not exceeding 5,000₣, or removal from position.

### Section 2: Offences Against Administrative Records and Integrity

#### Art. 21 Failure to log moderation actions
An Administrator who carries out a moderation action without recording the required entry in the official audit log or designated record within the prescribed timeframe is punished with a fine not exceeding 500₣.

#### Art. 22 Tampering with moderation logs
An Administrator who intentionally alters, falsifies, deletes, or conceals an official audit log, moderation record, or administrative entry is punished with a suspension, a fine not exceeding 5,000₣, or removal from position.

#### Art. 23 Bribery
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator who solicits, accepts, or promises to accept Nirleka francs, real-world currency, or any other personal advantage in exchange for performing or omitting an official administrative act is punished with removal from position and a fine of not less than 2,000₣.

<sup>2</sup> Whoever offers, promises, or grants an advantage to an Administrator to influence their official conduct is subject to penalties under ordinary Server law.

#### Art. 24 Abuse of power
An Administrator who intentionally uses their administrative position, access privileges, or technical powers to secure an unlawful advantage for themselves or a third party, or to intentionally cause harm to a member, is punished with a suspension, a fine not exceeding 5,000₣, or removal from position.

### Section 3: Offences Against Member Rights and Public Order

#### Art. 25 Unlawful moderation
An Administrator who intentionally imposes a ban, kick, timeout, or other restriction on a member without a factual basis or legal ground provided by Server law is punished with a timeout not exceeding 14 days, a fine not exceeding 2,500₣, or suspension.

#### Art. 26 Targeted harassment and personal hostility
An Administrator who uses their official position or public communication channels to repeatedly insult, intimidate, dox, or publish private personal details of a member or another Administrator without consent is punished with a suspension, a fine not exceeding 5,000₣, or removal from position.

#### Art. 27 Instigation of public disorder
An Administrator who publicly incites members to violate Server law, disobey administrative orders, or disrupt official Server functions is punished with a suspension or removal from position.

> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance with Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 101). Applies to all members of Administration.

---

## Chapter 1: Purpose and Scope

#### Art. 1 Purpose
The Administration Codes and subsequent laws govern the conduct of the Administration and its procedures.

#### Art. 2 Scope
The Administration Codes and subsequent laws apply to all members of Administration, including all Administrators holding positions defined in Chapter 2 of the Server Charter (SR 101) and their appointed staff.

## Chapter 2: General Provisions

### Section 1: Definitions and Principles

#### Art. 3 Definitions
<sup>1</sup> In this Code:

a. *Administrator* means any member of Administration or their appointed staff.

b. *moderation action* means any action taken to enforce rules or manage members, including:
  1. warnings;
  2. timeouts;
  3. kicks;
  4. bans;
  5. message deletions; and
  6. thread closures.

#### Art. 4 Principles
<sup>1</sup> Administrators must enforce all laws equally among all members of the Server.

<sup>2</sup> Administrators must maintain a peaceful, safe, and orderly environment for the Server while balancing individual liberty.

<sup>3</sup> During normal operations, Administrators are encouraged to maintain close relationships with members of the Server.

<sup>4</sup> During conflicts, Administrators must maintain professionalism and emotional distance.

<sup>5</sup> For any loopholes, flaws, or situations not specified in law or procedure, Administrators must act in good faith to uphold paragraph 2.

<sup>6</sup> Administrators must maintain full knowledge of the law and specified procedures.

<sup>7</sup> A judging authority must increase penalties for violations committed by senior Administrators.

### Section 2: Server Features

#### Art. 5 Server settings
The Director has the power to modify Server settings.

#### Art. 5a Bots
The Head Administrator and The Director have the authority to add, remove, or modify Server bots.

---

## Chapter 3: Specific Provisions and Compilations

### Section 1: Behaviours

#### Art. 6 Professional conduct
<sup>1</sup> Administrators must treat all members with respect.

<sup>2</sup> Art. 9 of the Public Code (SR 210) limits freedom of speech.

<sup>3</sup> Constant use of slurs, harassment, or tantrums incurs:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 7 Abuse of power
<sup>1</sup> Administrators must not exercise their powers for personal gain, irritation, pettiness, or spite.

<sup>2</sup> A violation of paragraph 1 incurs:
a. a 48-hour timeout on the first offence; and
b. removal from position on the second offence.

#### Art. 8 Negligence
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator must take action if available and aware that a violation of law is occurring.

<sup>2</sup> Failure to comply with paragraph 1 incurs:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 9 Bribery
Any Administrator who willingly accepts compensation from another individual in exchange for administrative influence must be removed from position and permanently barred from holding any position in Administration.

---

### Section 2: Exercise of Power and Documentation

#### Art. 10 Moderation actions
<sup>1</sup> All moderation actions and administrative acts must comply with applicable laws.

<sup>2</sup> A violation of paragraph 1 incurs:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

<sup>3</sup> A senior or superior Administrator must immediately reverse unlawful moderation decisions and actions.

<sup>4</sup> Actions taken in bad faith by Administrators that enabling laws do not explicitly provide for remain subject to paragraph 1.

#### Art. 11 Documentation of moderation actions
<sup>1</sup> Administrators must document all moderation actions according to the procedures outlined by the Head Administrator or Director.

<sup>2</sup> Failure to log a moderation action incurs:
a. a warning on the first offence;
b. a 48-hour timeout on the second offence; and
c. removal from position on the third offence.

#### Art. 12 Tampering with moderation logs
<sup>1</sup> An Administrator must not tamper with, deceptively modify, or delete moderation logs. A violation incurs:
a. a 48-hour timeout on the first offence; and
b. removal from position on the second offence.

<sup>2</sup> Log modifications resulting from clerical errors are exempt from paragraph 1.

#### Art. 13 Compromised accounts
<sup>1</sup> A user account is considered compromised if it performs any of the following:
a. sends unauthorised, automated, or deceptive communications, including phishing URLs, fraudulent promotional offers, or mass user mentions;
b. alters profile metadata, display names, or profile pictures to impersonate platform support personnel, Server staff, or system bots; or
c. initiates unauthorised administrative modifications, including creating rogue webhooks, escalating role privileges, or generating bulk invites.

<sup>2</sup> Upon encountering a user exhibiting behaviours specified in paragraph 1, an Administrator must immediately ban the user.

#### Art. 14 (Repealed)

laws.title: The Dokusai-kun and The Server
laws.content:
> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance with Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 101), by the Director

---

## Art. 1 Purpose
Dokusai-kun shall be the symbol and Dicktator of the server and its unity.

## Art. 2 Authority
Dokusai-kun remains subjected under the law and the Administration.

## Art. 3 Power
Dokusai-kun may exercise any power that the Administration does not restrict.

## Art. 4 Restriction on Powers
<sup>1</sup> Dokusai-kun shall not give roles to members that holds administrative permissions.

<sup>2</sup> Dokusai-kun shall not give any currency to another member.

<sup>3</sup> Dokusai-kun shall not delete a channel unilaterally.

## Art. 5 Passing the Crown
<sup>1</sup> If Dokusai-kun did not send a message or done an interaction in the last 90-days, the People may do a server-wide vote to replace Dokusai-kun with another member.

<sup>2</sup> Candidates of Dokusai-kun shall not have comitted any grave violations or predatory conduct.

<sup>3</sup> Dokusai-kun may declare to pass the crown onto another person. Said person is not exempt from paragraph 2's restriction.

## Art. 6 Impeachment
<sup>1</sup> Dokusai-kun shall be subject to impeachment.

<sup>2</sup> If 25% of the server's total active natural members are in favour of impeachment, Dokusai-kun shall be removed from position.

laws.title: The Culture Code Between the Director and Members of the Nirleka Studios Discord Server
laws.content:
> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance with Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 101), by the Director

---

### Art. 1 Cat Supremacy
The Cat is our Soupurreme Glorious Leadah.

### Art. 2 The Director
The Director possesses Soupurreme authority delegated by The Cat.

### Art. 3 Anonymity
Everyone shall have the right to anonymity.

### Art. 4 Humanity
Do not be a dick.

### Art. 5 Nuclear power
Nuclear power plants are among the most overcomplicated ways to boil water. Opposing nuclear power is an opposition against The Cat, and is blasphemy.

### Art. 6 Patience
And whoever is patient and forgives—indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.

### Art. 7 Trolling
Trolling, or in the current era that is also referred to as rage-baiting, shall not be taken seriously. It means they win. Follow Art. 6.

### Art. 8 Balance
<sup>1</sup> Everyone is equally worthless.

<sup>2</sup> Everyone is made from the hands of a single Creator.

<sup>3</sup> A mortal asserting superiority against another mortal on their natural characteristics is transgression against The Cat.

<sup>4</sup> Male and female, female and male, one needs another. One serves a specific purpose. Otherwise, humanity can not exist. To assert superiority over sex is transgression against The Cat.

### Art. 9 A Belief
<sup>1</sup> There is no compulsion in religion.

<sup>2</sup> The power to punish a mortal for a transgression against the Creator rests between the mortal and the Creator.

<sup>3</sup> Surely someone who believes that our Creator smiles on and rewards the deliberate killing and maiming of innocents believes in a cruel creator. That is not, it cannot be, the Creator of Humanity.

<sup>4</sup> Can a mortal truly follow the words of the Creator? Does one mortal's transgression stain the words of the Creator?

laws.title: The Economy Act
laws.content:
> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance with Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 101), by the Director

---

## Section 1: Currency and Issuing Authority

### Art. 1 Currency unit
<sup>1</sup> The currency of the Server is the Nirleka franc.

<sup>2</sup> The Nirleka franc may be denoted by `₣` or ***F R A N C S***.

### Art. 2 Issuing authority
<sup>1</sup> The Director may pay a sum of money to any member at the Director’s discretion.

<sup>2</sup> The Head Administrator and the Director each have the authority to impose a financial penalty on, or recover a sum from, a member who commits a violation in accordance with the law.

## Section 2: Income, Transactions, and Fines

### Art. 3 Income
<sup>1</sup> Members may receive a variable reward of not less than 5₣ and not more than 15₣ per message sent in a public channel, subject to a minimum interval restriction of 1 minute between qualifying rewards.

<sup>2</sup> Members serving in the Administration may receive an allowance of a fixed amount.

<sup>3</sup> Members serving in the Administration must not receive any financial remuneration or reward for moderation actions.

### Art. 4 Transactions
<sup>1</sup> Transactions of Nirleka francs in any way must only be restricted within the features of the server.

<sup>2</sup> Violating paragraph 1 incurs a 16000₣ fine and 48-hour timeout.

### Art. 6 Fines
The Administration may codify a fixed fine for violations of law.

laws.title: The Touch Grass Act
laws.content:
> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance with Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 101), by the Director

---

## Art. 1 Touching grass
A natural person touches grass if they are present outdoors, and is no lower from 500 meters away from their home.

## Art. 2 Reward for touching grass
<sup>1</sup> Members may be compensated for providing proof of touching grass.

<sup>2</sup> Members may receive a minimum of 250₣ to 660₣ for proof(s) per 1-hour period.

## Art. 3 Evidence
<sup>1</sup> Members are required to provide proof before compensation, through various means including but not limited to:
a. photos;
b. livestreams;
c. videos; or
d. GPS tracking.

<sup>2</sup> Proofs dated before August 2026 are invalid.

<sup>3</sup> Members must not submit a proof that was not taken by them or another individual that was with them.

## Art. 4 Touching grass fraud
<sup>1</sup> Members submitting a fake proof incurs:
a. a warning on the first offence; and
b. a 1-week timeout and a fine of ranging from 1200₣ to 10,000₣.

laws.title: The Corner Act
laws.content:
> **Enactment Notice:** Enacted in accordance with Chapter 4 of the Server Charter (SR 101), by the Director

---

## Art. 1 A corner
<sup>1</sup> A corner is a unique channel created specifically for a member and owned by the member.

<sup>2</sup> The owner of a corner reserves the right to talk in that corner and may prohibit other members from interacting in their corner.

<sup>3</sup> Members of Administration are exempt from paragraph 1 if they have reasonable means and intentions.

<sup>4</sup> The People ultimately owns the server and may order the archival of a corner.

<sup>5</sup> A corner must not be deleted permanently.

## Art. 2 Permanent corners
The following are designated as permanent corners and can not be removed or taxed:
a. `nirleka-corner`;
b. `error-corner`;
c. `faze-corner`; and
e. `ueef-corner`.

## Art. 3 Archival of corners
<sup>1</sup> An archived corner is put in the Public Archive category to remain hidden from the public but can be accessed by those who have Archive Access.

<sup>2</sup> Permissions of the archived corner must be sync to the Public Archive category.

### Art. 4 Existing corners
For existing corners, the owner of those corners must pay for their corner tax on 19 August 2026.

---

### Art. 5 Purchasing corners
<sup>1</sup> A member may purchase a new corner or restore their old one for 50,400₣.

<sup>2</sup> Members who have committed grave violations of law must not acquire any corners.

<sup>3</sup> Members who have purchased a corner must not purchase another corner.

<sup>4</sup> Once a member have purchased a new corner, a corner with their name or nickname followed by `-corner` is created, and put under the Text Channels category.

### Art. 6 Taxation of corners
<sup>1</sup> The Director taxes all non-permanent corners for 1,600₣ per week.

<sup>2</sup> The owner of a corner have 48 hours to compensate the tax once rent is due.

<sup>3</sup> If an owner fails to compensate for the tax, the corner must be archived.
